summary: The code is syntactically valid and imports are present, and it runs an agent-based simulation with messaging, social influence, purchasing, and simple enforcement. However, it does not implement many required entities, parameters, interactions, and metrics from the specification. Key parameter names are mismatched, policy timing is not modeled, several required metrics/validations are missing or incorrect, and some error handling is overly silent.

issues.description: Large mismatch with the required simulation design: missing entities (Household, multiple Retailers, PublicHealthAgency with policy schedule, MediaSource diversity), attributes (age, household_id, occupation, ideology, vaccination_status, etc.), behaviors (household norms, move_between_locations, respond_to_messaging variants), and interactions (household_norms, risk_feedback).
issues.location: Overall design across classes Person, Location, Retailer, PublicHealthAuthority/MediaOutlet, Simulation
issues.solution: Add the specified entities with their attributes and behaviors; implement household-level norms and sharing, multiple retailers with stock/price/restocking and rationing, richer person attributes (ideology, risk perception dynamics, fatigue), and interactions per spec.

issues.description: Parameter names and semantics differ from the specification, causing provided parameters to be ignored. Examples: time_horizon_days vs simulation_duration_days; average_degree vs avg_degree; rewiring_prob vs network_type/avg_degree/clustering; retailer_restock_rate vs restock_rate_per_day; rationing_policy vs rationing_limit_per_purchase; enforcement_probability vs specified values; mandate_start_day/mandate_end_day ignored.
issues.solution: Align parameter names to the spec exactly and map them properly. For network, implement small-world with avg_degree and clustering_coefficient; use simulation_duration_days/time_step_days; implement mandate_start_day/mandate_end_day; adopt initial_adoption_rate, initial_mask_inventory_mean/sd, etc.

issues.description: Policy dynamics not implemented: no mandate start/end, location-specific mandates do not change over time, enforcement probability/resources not scheduled; policy_effect_size cannot be computed as required.
issues.solution: Add time-varying mandate activation using mandate_start_day and mandate_end_day. Track enforcement_resources/fine_amount; compute policy_effect_size as differences in adoption before vs during and during vs after the mandate.

issues.description: Many required metrics are missing or incorrect: sustained_adoption_post_policy, compliance_by_location_type, policy_effect_size, stockouts_count (retailer-days), enforcement_costs, inequality across subgroups (e.g., ideology/income). Dynamic metrics mapping only covers a small subset and uses placeholders.
issues.location: Simulation.evaluate (metrics computation) and dynamic metrics block
issues.solution: Compute all required metrics: track adoption over time per location type; compute sustained_adoption_post_policy after mandate_end_day; track daily stockouts per retailer; aggregate enforcement costs (fines plus deployment if modeled); compute inequality across subgroups (income/ideology).

issues.description: Validations do not match the spec: convergence_check should compare change over the final 14 days with <1% threshold; s_curve_plausibility not assessed; no negative inventory validation for both retailers and agents.
issues.solution: Implement convergence_check using the last 14 days and absolute change < 0.01; add s-curve plausibility check (e.g., sigmoid-like fit or qualitative checks); validate that all inventories (retailer and agents) remain >= 0; include these results under 'validations'.

issues.description: Social and economic dynamics are oversimplified relative to spec: no homophily by ideology in network generation, no income constraint on purchases, no purchase intervals, no exogenous risk trend feedback, no location visibility factor.
issues.solution: Incorporate homophily by ideology when generating the network; include income/inventory constraints and purchase intervals; implement exogenous_risk_trend affecting local risk; use location visibility_factor to modulate social norm observation.

issues.description: Stockouts_count metric is computed as a single-day binary (end-of-run) rather than counting retailer-days with zero stock.
issues.solution: Track retailer stock at the end of each day and sum days where stock == 0; for multiple retailers, sum across all retailer-days.

issues.description: Convergence window set to 7 days and threshold 0.5% instead of the specified final 14 days and 1% threshold.
Compliance_by_location_type is returned as a single global placeholder, not stratified by location type (e.g., transit, retail, work).
issues.solution: Assign a type to each Location and track masked/total visits per type per day, then aggregate.

issues.description: Silent exception swallowing when writing results to file may hide I/O errors.
issues.solution: Log or print an error message to stderr when writing fails (e.g., use print to sys.stderr or logging).

issues.description: Person.belief_bias is never updated; bias_factor therefore remains fixed.
issues.solution: Update belief_bias over time based on media exposure or network influence, or remove it if not used.

issues.description: Purchase behavior lacks purchase interval and rationing limit from spec; people buy only just-in-time for a single mask, ignoring purchase_interval_days and rationing_limit_per_purchase.
issues.solution: Add a next_purchase_day per agent drawn from a distribution; use rationing_limit_per_purchase parameter; model desired quantities based on inventory and intervals.

issues.description: Odd indentation before an inline comment in Location.reset_daily_counters (likely harmless).
issues.solution: Remove or realign the stray comment to avoid style warnings.
